name: Mullvad
tagline: The only VPN that doesn't want to know who you are
highlights: Sign up with a randomly generated account number — no email required
Pay with cash, Monero, or Bitcoin for complete anonymity
Open source clients independently audited by Cure53
verdict: The gold standard for privacy — no affiliate programme, and we recommend it anyway.
bestFor: Anyone who takes privacy seriously and wants a VPN with no incentive to keep data about them

name: Proton VPN
tagline: Swiss-based, open source, free tier with no data limit
highlights: Switzerland jurisdiction: strong privacy laws, outside EU and intelligence alliances
Fully open source clients, audited in 2024 and 2025
Free tier with unlimited data — no ads, no throttling, no data sold
verdict: Swiss jurisdiction, open source, and the only trustworthy free VPN tier.
bestFor: Privacy-conscious users who want a free tier that doesn't monetise their data

name: Surfshark
tagline: Unlimited devices, budget price — owned by Nord Security
highlights: Unlimited simultaneous connections — cover every device in your household
Owned by Nord Security, same parent company as NordVPN
verdict: Best value for device coverage. Connection reliability has declined in 2025–2026.
bestFor: Users who need to cover many devices cheaply and accept occasional connection troubleshooting

name: NordVPN
tagline: The most recognised name in VPN — with a complicated history
highlights: PwC audit (2022) confirmed no-logs policy — credible independent verification
Panama jurisdiction: outside 14 Eyes, no mandatory data retention
4.5 stars from 1.28 million Play Store reviews
verdict: Reliable for mainstream use, but the 2018 breach and delayed disclosure are worth knowing.
bestFor: Mainstream users who want a reliable, well-supported VPN and don't need maximum privacy guarantees

name: ExpressVPN
tagline: Premium pricing, declining reliability, controversial ownership
highlights: Acquired by Kape Technologies in 2021 (formerly Crossrider, an adware company)
Highest price in the category — around $8–10/month on an annual plan
Long-term users report significant reliability decline in recent updates
verdict: The price premium is no longer justified. Kape ownership is a material concern.
bestFor: Users with specific streaming needs who were already on ExpressVPN and haven't hit reliability issues
